strings.name: Mark Rutte
strings.role: Politician · Former Dutch prime minister · NATO secretary general
strings.summary: Mark Rutte is a Dutch politician who studied history and worked in corporate personnel management before leading the VVD. Prime minister from 2010 to 2024, he headed four coalition governments through financial crisis, the pandemic and the childcare benefits scandal. He became NATO secretary general in 2024, promoting allied defence investment and transatlantic security coordination.
strings.coverageNote: Selected early life, Dutch premiership and the 2025 Hague summit; NATO office checked in November 2026. Spending targets are not recorded as achieved.
strings.influence.rationale: He served for many years as Dutch prime minister and entered NATO leadership, participating in joint European governance and transatlantic security coordination.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Long coalition leadership
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Led four Dutch coalitions from 2010 to 2024, becoming the country's longest-serving prime minister.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: NATO coordination
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Took NATO's secretary general post in 2024 and chaired the 2025 Hague summit's coordination of defence investment targets.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Hague summit adopts investment target
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Chaired the summit where allies committed to a combined 5% of GDP for core defence and related security spending by 2035.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Becomes NATO secretary general
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Succeeded Jens Stoltenberg as NATO's fourteenth secretary general after nearly fourteen years as Dutch prime minister.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Fourth cabinet resigns
strings.timeline.event-3.text: The coalition collapsed over migration policy; he then announced his departure from domestic politics and continued as caretaker prime minister.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Childcare scandal prompts resignation
strings.timeline.event-4.text: His cabinet resigned accepting political responsibility for wrongful childcare benefit recoveries, after tax authorities falsely accused many families of fraud.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: First becomes prime minister
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Formed a government after leading the VVD to election victory, then headed successive coalitions with different partners.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Leads the VVD
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Became VVD leader and parliamentary group leader, later taking the party to victory in the 2010 election.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Enters national government
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Moved from corporate personnel management to government as state secretary for social affairs and employment, later holding the education portfolio.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Graduates and joins Unilever
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Completed his history studies at Leiden and joined Unilever in personnel management, establishing his career before national politics.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Born in The Hague
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Born in The Hague in the Netherlands; he later completed secondary school there before studying history at Leiden University.
